targets_rule: the tier-2 design points as points in the four concepts' log10 changes; 16 vertices of their convex hull drawn without replacement (numpy default_rng(seed), from the sorted vertex indices); target = out x the vertex, rounded to 2 places

methods.lookup: the tier-2 design point with the smallest worst miss; no evaluations
methods.gmoo: queries on steer@12's model: every concept within tol of its target, uniq and coh at least the tier, drift at most drift_max; tol starts at start_factor x the lookup's miss and is multiplied by tighten whenever a query meets it; asked again at the same tol otherwise, until budget evaluations are used or a query returns no new evaluation. Its answer is its best tier-2 evaluation or the lookup's point, whichever misses less

score: the worst miss: the largest absolute log10 error over the four concepts, against the zero design on the same prompts
primary: on the training prompts, the number of the 16 profiles where globalMOO's worst miss is smaller than the lookup's by more than 0.001

prediction.arithmetic: In steer@12 the query beat the lookup in 6 of the 6 profiles where the lookup missed by 0.07 or more, and in 1 of the 10 where it missed by 0.04 or less: with room, it won every time. Here the lookup's miss on every one of the 16 targets is listed in lookup_miss, so by that rate all 16 have room. Two things cut it: the targets ask for changes 25% beyond anything the model was trained on, and the hull's vertices sit where the drift limit binds. About 6% of steer@12's 2,234 later tier-2 evaluations (18 of a sample of 320) fell outside the hull without being aimed there, so outside is reachable, but none of them comes closer to a 1.25x target than the lookup does. I discount the 6-of-6 rate to 0.7: 16 x 0.7 = 11.
prediction.held: 9 or more of 16 (more than half). A tie counts against. globalMOO cannot lose a profile, since its answer falls back to the lookup's point

reported: the same count on the 64 held-out prompts (smaller / larger / equal), the mean worst miss of both on both prompt sets, how many queries met their band, and how many query evaluations met tier 2
